references.text: Jesus elaborates on what it means to be born again: one must be born of water and the Spirit to enter the kingdom of God. [ref:Joh 3:5-7|John 3:5-7] is the direct continuation where Jesus explains the new birth he introduced in verse 3.
[ref:Joh 1:12-13|John 1:12-13] speaks of those who are born of God—not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, but of God. This is the theological foundation for the new birth Jesus mentions.

[ref:1 Pet 1:3|1 Peter 1:3] speaks of how God has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, which directly reflects the concept of being born again.
[ref:1 Pet 1:23|1 Peter 1:23] describes the new birth that happens through the living and enduring word of God, an elaboration on what it means to be born again.
[ref:Jak 1:18|James 1:18] says that God gave us birth according to his own will by the word of truth, which connects to the divine new birth Jesus speaks about.
[ref:1 Joh 3:9|1 John 3:9] refers to the one who is born of God and links the new birth to a new life in which one does not live in sin.
[ref:Tit 3:5|Titus 3:5] speaks of the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit—a key concept that complements Jesus' words about being born again.

[ref:2 Kor 5:17|2 Corinthians 5:17] says that if anyone is in Christ, they are a new creation; the old has passed away, behold, the new has come. This is Paul's parallel to Jesus' teaching on the new birth.
[ref:Gal 6:15|Galatians 6:15] emphasizes that what matters is being a new creation, which corresponds with the necessity of being born again.

[ref:Esek 36:25-27|Ezekiel 36:25-27] is an Old Testament prophecy about cleansing and a new spirit that God will place within his people—the background for Jesus' expectation that Nicodemus should understand the new birth (cf. v.10).
[ref:Sal 51:12|Psalm 51:12] is David's prayer that God would create in him a clean heart and renew a steadfast spirit—an Old Testament parallel to the need for a new birth from within.
[ref:Joh 3:31|John 3:31] uses the Greek word "ἄνωθεν" (from above), which is also used in 3:3, linking the new birth to something that comes from above, from heaven.
